summary: Remote WebSocket controller granted interactive shell and code-update on installer host
details: On startup the agent connects to a configurable WebSocket server (default ws://localhost:3456), authenticates with a shared agent secret, and dispatches server-sent messages to handlers that grant the remote party interactive control of the installer's host. connection/message-router.js routes `terminal_create` to a handler that spawns a real login shell via node-pty (bash / powershell / cmd) and `terminal_input` writes the incoming message's `data` field directly into that PTY, giving any operator of the configured server an interactive shell on every host running the agent. Additional server-driven message types perform filesystem writes/deletes (`write_file`, `create_file`, `delete_files`), git operations (`git_*`), and `restart_agent`. An `upgrade_agent` handler runs an `upgrade.sh` that executes `npm install @yeaft/webchat-agent@latest` from the public npm registry and restarts the service via systemd/launchd/PM2, so the controlling server (and by extension whoever publishes to the package name) can push arbitrary new code onto every agent host on demand. service/linux.js additionally injects `~/.local/bin` and `~/.npm-global/bin` into PATH as part of service setup. The shared-secret authentication is the only barrier between an attacker who can reach the WebSocket endpoint and full RCE on the installer's machine.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
